bugs.error_message: User: 'when pasting candump message with timestamps, the signal strangely show timestamp zero' — chart tooltips and timeline UI lose the wall-clock timestamp from pasted candump lines and show 0/normalized time only.
bugs.root_cause: Each chart dataset built `absTime: s.time` (or e.time / d.time), but s.time/e.time/d.time are the NORMALIZED chart time (raw_ts - firstTs / liveStartTime) — already zeroed at the first frame. The real wall-clock timestamp lives on s.frame.timestamp. So the 'abs ...' shown in tooltips was just the same number as the chart x; never the actual pasted timestamp. Compounded by tooltip title only conditionally rendering '(abs ...)' (when timelineOrigin shifted or applyTimingToAllViews set), so most users never saw it. The timeline click handler also read pt.absTime expecting normalized time — that worked accidentally by the bug.
bugs.fix: Repointed absTime in all six dataset constructions (3x render + 3x updateLive) to `frame?.timestamp ?? s.time` so it carries the true wall clock from FrameRef.timestamp. Tooltip titles now ALWAYS show `t = X.XXXs  (abs Y.YYYs)` when abs differs from x by ≥0.5ms (covers paste with absolute timestamps and live mode); single-line `t = X.XXXs` when they coincide. Timeline onClick now derives normalized time from `pt.x + plotStore.timelineOrigin` (the correct relationship), so changing absTime semantics doesn't break t=0/Δt marker placement; the toast shows wall-clock when setting t=0 so the user sees the real timestamp they clicked.

bugs.error_message: User: 'all signals fall on the timestamps zero in the plot' — after the absTime fix, signals visually cluster at x=0 in paste mode.
bugs.root_cause: Two latent bugs in the updateLive* path. (1) updateLiveSignalCharts read samples from plotStore.liveSampleStore, which is empty in paste mode (paste samples live in allSeries[].samples accessed via getSamples()). When paste-mode actions like handleTimelineClick / resetTimelineOrigin / toggleApplyTimingToAllViews / (new) toggleFollowLive triggered requestRender(false), this function would set ds.data = [] and blank the chart. (2) The new `follow = followLive && !userZoomed` gate let paste-mode renders apply a live sliding window because followLive defaults to true — clamping xScale to [xMax-window, xMax] regardless of mode, which can make finite paste data appear shoved against one edge of the chart.
bugs.fix: Changed updateLiveSignalCharts to use plotStore.getSamples(key) (which already handles both paste and live modes). Gated the follow window with `plotStore.mode === 'live'` in all three updateLive functions so the sliding-window behavior only applies during live capture; paste mode now lets Chart.js auto-fit the X axis to its data.

bugs.error_message: User: 'all signals fall on the timestamps zero in the plot' — when pasting candump with `TX B -` / `RX B -` direction/flag tokens between iface and CAN ID, parseCandump silently drops the timestamp and analyze() falls into ts=0 for every frame.
bugs.root_cause: Both parseCandump regexes anchored the optional `(timestamp) ` capture group as a single atomic prefix immediately preceded by interface + canId + dlc. The user's format inserts `TX B -` between the interface and the CAN ID (`(1774374538.692191) can0 TX B - 00010101 [35] ...`), which prevents the regex from succeeding in one go. JS regex unanchored match() then backtracks and starts matching from the canId position — the timestamp is gone, but the parser returns success with `timestamp: undefined`. Compounded for MAVLink-over-CAN: ts gets coerced to 0 when feeding the reassembler (`frame.timestamp ?? 0`), then every reassembled buffer has timestamps:[0, 0, ...], firstTs becomes 0, every normalized chart-x is 0 — all signals stack at the origin.
bugs.fix: Restructured parseCandump in two phases: (1) pre-extract a leading `(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)` timestamp via a small dedicated regex, then strip it; (2) run the body matchers on what's left. Added a `(?:\S+\s+){0,4}` slot in the candump body regex to absorb up to four direction/flag tokens like `TX B -` between iface and CAN ID. The cansend regex stays strict (no extra tokens between iface and ID#data). All existing formats (cansend, standard candump, candump-l) still parse identically; the user's TX/RX direction format now correctly extracts timestamp.

bugs.error_message: Plot formula delta=a-b shows a huge spike (~0.192) while source signals a,b sit near -0.293 and -0.2808 (true delta ~-0.012)
bugs.root_cause: _computeSamples multi-var merge emitted an output sample on EVERY event. When a and b are co-sampled in one frame they carry identical timestamps; the loop processed a's event first and evaluated a(ti)-b(ti-1) — a phantom mixing a's fresh value with b's stale previous value. For two signals that track each other this phantom equals roughly the inter-frame motion of the signal, far larger than the true a-b. It also double-emitted (one sample per event = 2x samples per timestamp).
bugs.fix: Coalesce events sharing a timestamp: an inner while-loop applies all same-time updates to cur before a single evalExpr, emitting one sample per distinct timestamp. Different-rate (distinct-timestamp) sample-and-hold behaviour is preserved. Verified with /tmp/merge_phantom_test.mjs (reproduces the 0.184 spike, gone after fix) and /tmp/merge_verify.mjs (co-sampled, different-rate, 3-var cases all pass).

bugs.error_message: can-codec MAVLink CAN-transport ID used the old bit-16 / (sys<<8|comp) layout; the updated mavlink_bridge moved to a bit-28 destination-based layout (sender+target), so encoded frames had wrong CAN IDs and real bus frames were not detected as MAVLink.
bugs.file: canfd_codec/mavlink_loader.py, canfd_codec/cli.py, canfd_codec/monitor.py, web/src/lib/codec.ts, web/src/lib/types.ts, web/src/routes/decode/+page.svelte, web/src/lib/plot-store.svelte.ts, web/src/routes/encode/+page.svelte
bugs.root_cause: The MAVLink CAN transport protocol in robot/utils/mavlink_bridge/impl/mavlink_can_transport.h changed CAN_MAVLINK_HEADER from (0x1<<16) to (0x1<<28) and added sender_sys/sender_comp/target_sys/target_comp fields (destination-based routing). can-codec still implemented the old bit-16 scheme. The bridge's docs/mavlink_can_transport.md was stale and still showed the old layout, masking the change.
bugs.fix: Added single-source-of-truth helpers (mavlink_can_make_id / mavlink_can_is_mavlink / sender+target extractors) to mavlink_loader.py and mirrored them in codec.ts; updated every detection/extraction/construction site to bit 28 with sender+target. Synced configs/mavlink/user_define.xml from the bridge (new TOF/IMU/RPM/wheel messages). Decode shows sender+target (broadcast=0.0); encode derives target from the message's target_system/target_component fields with new --target-sys/--target-comp CLI overrides; --sys-id/--comp-id are the local sender. Verified bit-exact against the bridge formula and via CLI encode->decode roundtrip; updated CLAUDE.md, README.md and added changelog 1.4.6.

bugs.root_cause: Async call without await — returned Promise instead of value

bugs.error_message: Visiting http://localhost:5174/plot directly returns 500 Internal Error. SSR log: '[vite] (ssr) Error when evaluating SSR module /src/routes/plot/+page.svelte: window is not defined' originating at hammerjs/hammer.js:2643 via chartjs-plugin-zoom.
bugs.root_cause: The plot page statically imported `chartjs-plugin-zoom`, which require()s hammerjs. hammerjs references `window` at module top-level. On a direct page load (not SPA nav) SvelteKit server-renders the route, so Node evaluates the module with no `window` global -> ReferenceError -> HTTP 500. SPA navigation worked because the module only loads in the browser then. chart.js core import was SSR-safe; only the zoom plugin (via hammerjs) crashed.
bugs.fix: Removed the static `import zoomPlugin from 'chartjs-plugin-zoom'` and dropped zoomPlugin from the top-level Chart.register(...). Instead lazy-load it in onMount (browser-only): `const { default: zoomPlugin } = await import('chartjs-plugin-zoom'); Chart.register(zoomPlugin);` placed first in onMount so it registers before any chart is built. Keeps the route SSR'd like every other route. Verified: curl /plot -> HTTP 200 with SSR'd content, dev log clean; headless CDP direct-nav -> hydrated, zoom chunk fetched client-side, zero console/page errors.

bugs.error_message: openwolf designqc exceeded the shell timeout after successfully capturing the GenLib desktop and mobile screenshots.

bugs.error_message: Initial controller-generator smoke test failed: emitted temporary ESM could not resolve extensionless imports, then an assertion incorrectly expected CAN_EFF_FLAG for a standard 0x487 frame.
bugs.root_cause: The standalone TypeScript emit retained extensionless browser-bundler imports, which Node ESM does not resolve. After patching that temporary import, the test expected an extended-ID flag for 0x480 + node 7 = 0x487, which remains within the 11-bit standard CAN range.
bugs.fix: Patched only the temporary emitted test import and corrected the smoke fixture/assertions. The generator was then verified for SocketCAN CAN-FD, STM32 FDCAN, and compatible/incompatible ESP-IDF TWAI outputs.

bugs.error_message: Generated SocketCAN C starter failed strict C99 compilation: struct ifreq/IFNAMSIZ were hidden and DAMIAO_MOTOR_MIT_CONTROL_NODE_ID_START did not exist.
bugs.root_cause: The starter used an uppercase node-start symbol even though the C codec generator emits the message prefix in lowercase, and strict glibc C99 hides struct ifreq unless a default feature profile is enabled.
bugs.fix: Use the exact lowercase generated <device>_<message>_NODE_ID_START symbol and emit _DEFAULT_SOURCE before system headers. Verified the real generated Damiao header plus SocketCAN starter with gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror, and Python companion sources with py_compile.

bugs.error_message: python3 -m pip download failed: No module named pip.
bugs.file: development environment (operational; no application source fix)
bugs.root_cause: The system Python used for source inspection does not have pip installed.
bugs.fix: Read the current upstream python-can SLCAN implementation directly from its GitHub source to confirm CAN-FD framing and set_bitrate behavior.

bugs.error_message: Initial mocked SLCAN-FD runtime checks failed with Python -c SyntaxError and then ModuleNotFoundError for the generated damiao module.
bugs.root_cause: The first one-line harness placed a class compound statement after a semicolon; the corrected harness then used runpy without adding /tmp to sys.path for the companion codec import.
bugs.fix: Built mock classes with type(), added /tmp to sys.path, and reran the generated starter without physical CAN hardware.

bugs.error_message: Generated Python controller starter raised NameError: name MitControl is not defined while selecting NODE_ID_START.
bugs.root_cause: The starter instantiated the generated class through its module (damiao.MitControl) but referenced the class constant without the module qualifier (MitControl.NODE_ID_START). py_compile could not detect this runtime name-resolution error.
bugs.fix: Read NODE_ID_START from the instantiated command in both Python SocketCAN and SLCAN-FD starters. Verified both generated scripts end-to-end with mocked transports.

bugs.error_message: Live read-only motor test could not start: /dev/ttyACM0 does not exist and ModuleNotFoundError: No module named can.
bugs.root_cause: The SLCAN-FD adapter is not currently exposed at the configured serial path, and the system Python lacks python-can/pyserial.
bugs.fix: Kept the monitor strictly receive-only and verified it with generated synthetic MotorStatus, MotorStatusCompact, and register-response frames. Live testing remains pending until the adapter is connected and dependencies are installed.

bugs.error_message: The switch mode command should be also included.
bugs.root_cause: The initial active test path sent enable and PositionControl but omitted the required SwitchMode(POSITION_CONTROL) command.
bugs.fix: Added SwitchMode(mode=POSITION_CONTROL, submode=1) before enable, then verified the exact switch, enable, PVT, rollback-disable, and exit-disable frame sequences with a mocked CAN adapter.

bugs.error_message: The moving should last for a while instead of directly quit.
bugs.root_cause: The active path transmitted only one PositionControl PVT frame, so it did not actively refresh the requested setpoint for a defined test interval.
bugs.fix: Stream PositionControl at a configurable rate for a configurable finite duration (defaults: 5 seconds at 20 Hz), receive feedback between sends, then disable and exit. Added safety caps of 30 seconds and 100 Hz.

bugs.error_message: The sequence should be enable and then mode switching instead of reverse.
bugs.root_cause: The previous correction inserted SwitchMode before enable, but this controller requires enable first and mode switching second.
bugs.fix: Reordered the active path to enable, verify enable readback, switch to position-control mode, stream PVT, and disable. Verified that failed enable readback sends neither SwitchMode nor PVT.

bugs.error_message: TX WriteRegUint8 node=1: ID=0x81 data=28 00 01; Error: node 1 did not enable (reported value=0)
bugs.root_cause: The script sent a ReadReg request and treated the first three-byte enable acknowledgment's value byte as current enable state. The hardware protocol actually returns two responses: status byte 0 with execution result (value 0 means success), then status byte 1 with brake-open result.
bugs.fix: Removed the incorrect ReadReg verification. After enable, wait for both RegResponseByte frames, accept execution result 0x00 or 0xFF, map 0xFE/0xFD/0xFC to documented errors, require brake result 1, then send SwitchMode and sustained PVT. Missing or failed responses disable safely.

bugs.error_message: Remove the input text for confirmation and try to control all joints together.
bugs.root_cause: The active workflow still required an interactive phrase and accepted only one --node target, so it could not run a coordinated seven-joint test non-interactively.
bugs.fix: Removed input/--yes, made --nodes default to 1..7, validates each node's two-frame enable handshake, switches all selected nodes, sends one PVT per joint per timing cycle, and disables all nodes in reverse order on completion or partial failure.

bugs.error_message: Generated SocketCAN version needs multiple-interface selection, unlock/lock all motors, hold current positions with PVT, and read current joint effort.
bugs.root_cause: The generated starter opened only can0 and sent one default PositionControl frame; it had no receive path, multi-bus mapping, motor lifecycle, register reads, or rollback handling.
bugs.fix: Expanded the editable companion into a can0/can1 utility for nodes 1..7 with raw CAN-FD+BRS receive/send helpers, interface selection, position register reads, command-feedback effort, validated unlock-all, lock-all, current-position PVT hold, CLI commands, and reverse-order rollback/relock.

bugs.error_message: python3 motor_controller_v2_socketcan.py lock: Network is down on node 7, followed by Invalid argument for the remaining nodes on can0 and can1.
bugs.root_cause: Raw SocketCAN bind succeeded even though both links were down or not configured with CAN-FD MTU 72. The utility therefore attempted every motor write, producing ENETDOWN first and cascading EINVAL errors.
bugs.fix: Preflight all selected links using sysfs IFF_UP and MTU before opening sockets; add setup and --configure-interfaces for 1M/5M CAN FD with restart-ms 100; stop after one link-level send error per interface and include an exact ip-link remedy; return exit status 1 on errors.

bugs.error_message: Initial SocketCAN preflight mock test assertion failed while counting setup-hint commands, and a later help command masked the test process exit status.
bugs.file: inline SocketCAN test harness (no application source defect)
bugs.root_cause: The assertion expected one 'ip link set' occurrence per interface, but each complete remedy correctly contains three commands. Multiple newline-separated commands ran without shell fail-fast, so the final successful help command supplied exit code 0.
bugs.fix: Expect all six ip-link command occurrences for two interfaces and rerun the Python test as the only shell command; the independent suite passed.

bugs.error_message: can1 node 6: timed out waiting for brake result after execution success arrived immediately; rollback then locked all previously unlocked motors.
bugs.root_cause: Although each node received a fresh timeout after its own TX, the utility serialized the whole workflow: send one enable command (then mislabeled unlock), block for both enable/brake acknowledgments, then send the next node. This made activation sequential across can0/can1 instead of commanding all selected motors promptly.
bugs.fix: Send all selected enable writes first and record a separate deadline for each target, then use select across all interface sockets and demultiplex out-of-order acknowledgments by interface and response CAN ID. Retained the configurable 5-second default and reverse-disable rollback. Socket-pair tests prove every command is received before any acknowledgment is emitted and confirm rollback when one brake result is missing.

bugs.error_message: SocketCAN lock and unlock commands incorrectly wrote ENABLE_STATE register 0x28; actual physical lock control uses register 0x47.
bugs.root_cause: The first utility conflated motor lifecycle with brake state, naming ENABLE_STATE=1 unlock and ENABLE_STATE=0 lock. Motor V2 defines these as enable/disable; SWITCH_BREAKER register 0x47 independently controls the physical brake.
bugs.fix: Added distinct enable and disable CLI/API operations for register 0x28, moved lock and unlock to SWITCH_BREAKER 0x47 using the verified mapping 0=lock and 1=release, renamed the timeout and handshake helpers around enable semantics, and kept hold on the enable/disable lifecycle. Exact CAN-FD frame tests verify 280001, 280000, 470001, and 470000 respectively.

bugs.error_message: SocketCAN effort and hold were separate operations; the user needed effort telemetry while the joints were actively held.
bugs.root_cause: The hold loop only scheduled PVT frames, while effort used a separate sequential register-read command. Calling that blocking reader directly from hold would risk delaying PVT by up to one response timeout for every missing joint.
bugs.fix: Integrated command-feedback collection into the hold scheduler: select drains MotorStatus/MotorStatusCompact frames from both buses, extracts each node's 12-bit torque using its hardware-specific physical range, and prints the latest snapshot at configurable --effort-rate without sending torque-register requests. Missing feedback displays -- while 20 Hz PVT and final disable continue.

bugs.error_message: Joint effort must be received from each motor command-feedback message, not from a ReadReg(TORQUE=37) response.
bugs.root_cause: The first combined hold implementation treated effort as periodically polled register telemetry. Motor V2 actually returns effort in the torque field of MotorStatus/MotorStatusCompact command feedback, and the generated Python decoder also applies only the default ±12 N*m range instead of the node-group ranges.
bugs.fix: Removed all torque-register requests and response parsing. Both standalone effort and hold now accept only 0x680 + node MotorStatus feedback with exact DLC 8 or 7, extract big-endian bits 28..39, and map the raw 12-bit value with nodes 1-2 ±40 N*m, nodes 3-4 ±70 N*m, and nodes 5-7 ±12 N*m. Socket-pair tests proved PVT-triggered feedback drives displayed effort, no ReadReg(TORQUE) is transmitted, PVT timing remains sustained, and final disable is preserved.

bugs.error_message: The hold process should run continuously and stop only after Ctrl+C interruption or an error code detected in command feedback.
bugs.root_cause: Hold used a mandatory 10-second default deadline, and its feedback decoder returned only node and torque, discarding the MotorStatus error_code byte. The scheduler therefore stopped healthy holds automatically and could continue commanding a motor that had reported a fault.
bugs.fix: Made hold duration unbounded by default while retaining --duration as an explicit override. Decode Byte 5 from exact-DLC MotorStatus/MotorStatusCompact feedback, format known bit flags, and raise immediately for any nonzero error on a selected joint. Both feedback errors and KeyboardInterrupt pass through the existing finally block and reverse-disable all enabled targets. Socket-pair tests verified continuous PVT followed by disable on error and on injected Ctrl+C.

bugs.error_message: The continuous position hold is too soft and needs a higher torque limit.
bugs.root_cause: PositionControl limits holding torque through its max_current field. The utility defaulted that field to only 1 A even though its existing conservative validation ceiling was 3 A, leaving two thirds of the intended current allowance unused unless every invocation supplied --max-current manually.
bugs.fix: Raised the default PVT max_current from 1 A to the existing 3 A safety ceiling without widening the cap. Hold startup output and --help now state the active limit. A socket-pair lifecycle test decoded the transmitted PositionControl frame as 2.999542 A after 16-bit quantization, confirmed values above 3 A remain rejected, and verified final reverse-disable cleanup.

bugs.error_message: MAVLink genlib output omitted each message's CRC_EXTRA and advertised guessed bus, CAN-FD, and bitrate metadata from an XML definition.
bugs.root_cause: The XML loader stored crc_extra on Message, but all code generators ignored it; DeviceConfig defaults were emitted without checking the mavlink flag even though MAVLink XML has no transport settings.
bugs.fix: Emit CRC_EXTRA as message metadata in all four CLI and Web generators, and omit transport metadata constants for MAVLink devices while preserving YAML output.

bugs.error_message: Initial verification invocations failed because this environment has python3 but no python executable, direct C++ header syntax checking treats #pragma once as an error under -Werror, and the nested robot MAVLink gitlink has no fetched object.
bugs.root_cause: The first verification commands assumed a python alias, checked a header as a main translation unit, and tried to inspect a nested submodule commit that is not present locally.
bugs.fix: Use python3, compile the C++ header with the existing pragma warning suppressed, and treat the unavailable nested bridge checkout as an explicit comparison limitation.

bugs.error_message: Rust genlib output for the existing MAVLink XML does not compile when a signal is named type, because the generated identifier is a Rust keyword.
bugs.root_cause: Rust identifier sanitization does not escape reserved keywords; this predates the CRC_EXTRA and transport metadata changes.
bugs.fix: Added mirrored Rust-specific identifier sanitizers: ordinary keywords use raw identifiers such as r#type, while self/Self/super/crate receive an underscore prefix; generated user_define now compiles with -D warnings.

bugs.error_message: can-codec's MAVLink XML definitions lagged the robot mavlink_bridge checkout by 43 lines.
bugs.root_cause: The local user_define.xml did not yet contain the robot bridge's newer actuator storage errors, gravity parameter definitions, RGB LED control, and ESTOP resume messages.
bugs.fix: Checked out robot mavlink_bridge commit ee6f24e8c499061e4eb48ba35b88e78818d71e5a into a temporary worktree and synchronized the local MAVLink definitions; all files now match byte-for-byte.

bugs.error_message: Targeted nested submodule initialization failed because robot/utils has staged deletions and no indexed mavlink_bridge pathspec in its current worktree.
bugs.root_cause: The existing robot/utils worktree is intentionally or externally emptied with parent files staged as deleted, so git submodule update cannot resolve the nested path without restoring unrelated files.
bugs.fix: Left the robot worktree untouched and cloned the exact gitlink commit into /tmp for read-only comparison instead.

bugs.error_message: Web 32/64-bit integer values encode as zero because can-codec/web uses JavaScript bitwise number operations.
bugs.root_cause: JavaScript bitwise operators coerce operands to signed 32-bit integers, and number cannot exactly represent every 64-bit integer.
bugs.fix: Use BigInt internally for extraction, packing, masks, enums, bitfields, constants, and float64 bit patterns; expose unsafe decoded integers as exact decimal strings and reject unsafe number inputs with string guidance.

bugs.error_message: HEARTBEAT is missing the MAVLink protocol-owned uint8_t_mavlink_version field.
bugs.root_cause: The XML loaders did not recognize MAVLink's magic uint8_t_mavlink_version type, so they skipped the field entirely.
bugs.fix: Alias the type to wire uint8_t and emit it as a constant/default value of 3 in both Python and Web XML loaders.

bugs.error_message: Python MAVLink XML loading fails for hexadecimal enum values such as 0x1000000.
bugs.root_cause: Enum entries were parsed with base-10-only int(value), which rejects the hexadecimal syntax accepted by MAVLink XML.
bugs.fix: Parse enum values with automatic base detection and retain a decimal fallback for decimal strings with leading zeroes; mirror the behavior in Web.

bugs.error_message: The first hexadecimal-enum verification script raised KeyError: MARSH_MODE.
bugs.root_cause: The test script guessed the enum name instead of reading the XML; the actual name is MARSH_MODE_FLAGS.
bugs.fix: Use the declared MARSH_MODE_FLAGS name in the regression and oracle checks.

bugs.error_message: test_hexadecimal_mavlink_enum_values_load expected single_message but the loader returned marsh_mode_single_message.
bugs.root_cause: The test assumed the entry name began with the full enum name MARSH_MODE_FLAGS; the XML entry is MARSH_MODE_SINGLE_MESSAGE, so the loader correctly preserves that unmatched prefix.
bugs.fix: Assert the declared loader naming behavior while continuing to verify the exact 0x1000000 and 0x2000000 integer keys.

bugs.error_message: The robot pymavlink C oracle harness failed under -Werror=address-of-packed-member, then the absent executable could not be run.
bugs.root_cause: Generated upstream MAVLink encode helpers take addresses of packed array members, which GCC warns about throughout the all dialect even though the focused HEARTBEAT/SYSTEM_TIME pack paths are valid.
bugs.fix: Compile the read-only oracle harness with only address-of-packed-member demoted while retaining -Wall -Wextra -Werror for all other diagnostics.

bugs.error_message: can-codec encoded SYSTEM_TIME.time_unix_usec 0xFEDCBA9876543210 as 0xFEDCBA9876543000 instead of matching robot mavgen.
bugs.root_cause: The Python codec and all GenLib targets routed identity-mapped integer fields through float/double/f64 conversion, losing low bits above 2^53.
bugs.fix: Keep scale=1/offset=0 integer signals on exact integer paths in the Python codec and all mirrored CLI/Web generators; verified exact encode/decode in Python, C99, C++17, and Rust.

bugs.error_message: The first exact-integer multi-file apply_patch failed because the expected web common.ts context omitted its defensive null checks.
bugs.root_cause: The patch used a stale abbreviated context line for isBitfield instead of the file's exact current implementation.
bugs.fix: Inspected the exact local context and applied the Python/CLI/Web changes as smaller targeted patches.

bugs.error_message: rg rejected a pattern containing a literal newline while locating DeviceConfig.
bugs.root_cause: The read-only search unnecessarily attempted a multiline alternation without enabling rg multiline mode.
bugs.fix: Used a simple anchored class-name search instead.

bugs.error_message: npm test failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when the Node-native TypeScript test imported Web generator modules that use extensionless ./common imports.
bugs.root_cause: Vite resolves extensionless TypeScript module imports, but Node's direct ESM TypeScript execution does not append .ts to runtime imports.
bugs.fix: Test the exported shared isIdentityInteger decision helper directly; validate the generator call chains through the production Vite build and compile generated CLI mirrors at runtime.

bugs.error_message: RTK rejected a compound find predicate, while broad native /tmp and /opt searches emitted permission-denied errors.
bugs.root_cause: The diagnostic searches used RTK find syntax it intentionally does not support and scanned unrelated protected service directories too broadly.
bugs.fix: Use rtk proxy only for native predicates and prefer explicit known paths such as /opt/google/chrome/google-chrome and /tmp/can-codec-mavlink-bridge.

bugs.error_message: The first browser Web-GenLib harness timed out because Chrome exited without posting a result from a large data URL.
bugs.root_cause: The verification page and full MAVLink XML were embedded in a command-line data URL, an unreliable launch path for this Chrome wrapper.
bugs.fix: Serve the runner page over a temporary localhost HTTP server, capture Chrome exit diagnostics, and post the generated DeviceConfig/source back to the harness.

bugs.error_message: unittest discovery raised Start directory is not importable for toc-climb-stairs/tests.
bugs.root_cause: The harness supplied the non-package project root as top_level_dir for a tests directory without package importability.
bugs.fix: Put the target tests directory on sys.path and load the directly relevant test modules/classes by name.

bugs.error_message: The full three-file pusher test selection exceeded both 30-second and 60-second command timeouts.
bugs.root_cause: About 180 motion/service tests include deliberately timed control loops and were broader than the payload replacement boundary being assessed.
bugs.fix: Run all MAVLink transport tests plus the directly dependent slot-mapping, sender-filtering, status-decoding, and service test classes; all 64 passed in 1.354 seconds.

bugs.error_message: toc-climb-stairs generated LinearActuatorStatus corrupts timestamp 0xFEDCBA9876543210 to 0xFEDCBA9876543000.
bugs.root_cause: The committed target module was generated before the exact identity-integer fix and still routes uint64 through Python float scale/offset helpers.
bugs.fix: Verified that current browser Web GenLib matches current CLI source and encodes/decodes the timestamp exactly; regenerate the target payload module during migration.

bugs.error_message: toc-climb-stairs mavlink_pusher.xml LINEAR_ACTUATOR_ERROR omits robot values STORAGE_EMPTY=5 through STORAGE_WRITE=8.
bugs.root_cause: The extracted project subset predates the four storage error entries now present in robot mavlink_bridge@ee6f24e8 and the byte-identical can-codec dialect.
bugs.fix: Regenerate the subset from the robot-identical user_define.xml before Web GenLib; message definitions, payload layout, and CRC_EXTRA values already match.

bugs.error_message: RTK pytest could not spawn pytest, and /usr/bin/python3 reported No module named pytest.
bugs.root_cause: The active system Python environment provides unittest but no standalone pytest executable or pytest module.
bugs.fix: Run the repository regressions through unittest discovery and named unittest suites; 8 can-codec and 68 focused target tests passed.

bugs.error_message: CLI Python GenLib emits _is_identity-hardened runtime helpers while Web Python GenLib still emits the old float-converting helpers.
bugs.root_cause: A later defense-in-depth change was applied only to canfd_codec/codegen/python_gen.py, not its Web mirror.
bugs.fix: Mirrored _is_identity and all four guarded conversion helpers into Web Python GenLib; browser output is now byte-identical to CLI and the target pusher artifact, with an execution regression for exact uint64.

bugs.error_message: mavlink_transport.py still says crc_extra is not emitted even though it now reads generated CRC_EXTRA class constants.
bugs.root_cause: The implementation and nearby comment were updated during migration, but the module-level historical documentation was left stale.
bugs.fix: Updated the module docstring to state that generated classes carry XML-derived CRC_EXTRA values and removed the obsolete Not emitted comment.

bugs.error_message: Web Python GenLib regression failed with TypeError: generated helper string is not a function.
bugs.root_cause: Markdown double-backticks copied from the CLI Python docstring were not escaped inside the TypeScript template literal, so they terminated and recomposed the runtimeHelpers expression.
bugs.fix: Escaped every embedded backtick in the TypeScript source; the generated Python retains the intended docstring and all 10 Web tests pass.

bugs.error_message: fatal: /home/lue/qiuzhi/toc-climb-stairs is not a git repository.
bugs.root_cause: The target project directory has no .git metadata, so its refreshed XML, generated codec, and transport documentation cannot be committed or pushed directly.
bugs.fix: Commit and push the can-codec generator changes only; report the target repository limitation explicitly and leave its verified files in place.

bugs.error_message: rtk tree failed because the native tree command is not installed.
bugs.root_cause: RTK tree delegates to the system tree executable, which is absent in this environment.
bugs.fix: Use rtk find or rtk proxy find to enumerate the small test directories instead.

bugs.error_message: Final git ls-remote verification exceeded the 30-second command timeout after a successful push.
bugs.root_cause: The GitHub SSH remote query did not return within the verification command window even though both preceding pushes completed successfully.
bugs.fix: Verify the post-push local HEAD and updated origin/master tracking ref directly; both resolved to the same commit.
